Priya: Quick heads-up — I need to swap who is primary for the overnight window tonight. Sam put in PTO so there's a coverage gap from ~00:30-03:00 UTC. I'm reducing alert noise and handing primary to @Jordan for the 00:00-08:00 UTC rotation.
Jordan: OK I can take primary. Who's secondary?
Priya: @Alex will be secondary. Escalation order: Jordan -> Alex -> Priya. If page doesn't respond in 10m, escalate to OpsPager.
Priya: Reason: we've been getting a spike of KV-cache-evict p95 alerts that are noisy and correlate with a noisy batch job ramp. They're not user-facing errors but are generating a lot of pages. I want to temporarily raise the threshold and enable short suppression so we don't burn through pages overnight.
Jordan: Can you post the exact change so SRE/infra know what to expect? I want to be able to reverse quickly if things look off.
Priya: Yup. Applying a temporary suppression and threshold bump for the kv-evict policy:
```bash
# temporary update - revert in 6h unless we see regressions
monctl alerts update --id=kv-evict-p95 --threshold 0.06 --suppress 3600 --meta note="overnight coverage adjust by Priya"
```
Priya: Also increasing the incident-bot debounce for that policy so we only page on sustained regressions.
Maria: Adding runbook pointers: if you see sustained evictions + latency increase > 200ms, follow runbook steps 2-5 (reindex cache shards, check batch job QPS, drain problematic pool). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-evict
Alex: Got it. I'll watch logs for the batch job at /services/batch-runner and keep an eye on the routing table. If we see user-facing 500s, escalate immediately — don't wait for suppression to expire.
Jordan: Copy. I'll also enable token-level tracing for any incoming error spikes to help triage quickly.
OpsBot: alert-policy-update recorded: id=kv-evict-p95 changed by Priya; threshold=0.06; suppression=3600s; scheduled_revert=2141617200; audit_id=ap-67891
incident-bot: SLO suppression applied for kv-evict-p95 by Priya. Pager routing will be muted for this policy for 3600s. To force a page, include --force in incident CLI.
Sam: Sorry team — PTO caught me. Thanks for covering. Ping me if you need me to jump in before EOD my side.
Jordan: A couple of quick operational reminders: 1) If user error rate > 0.5% we cut suppression immediately and page; 2) If uptime SLO for inference endpoints drops > 0.2pp we trigger full-bridge.
Priya: I'll add a short pinned note in the oncall channel with the escalation ladder, runbook links, and the CLI snippet to revert:
```bash
monctl alerts update --id=kv-evict-p95 --threshold 0.03 --suppress 0 --meta note="revert overnight adjustment"
```
Priya: Thanks @Jordan @Alex @Maria. I'll monitor for the next 30m and keep the team posted. If anyone sees anything weird DM me directly. :thumbsup:
Jordan: Acknowledged. I'll be primary from 00:00 UTC.
Alex: Acknowledged secondary.
Maria: Monitoring dashboards up (kv-evict, inference-latency, user-errors). Will flag anomalies in this thread.
OpsBot: Reminder scheduled: revert-alert-policy job set for 2141617200 (6h).
incident-bot: Log entry added to incident ledger: temporary policy change for noise suppression by Priya; link=https://redwood.internal/incidents/ledger/3456
Priya: Closing loop — I'll post a short postmortem if suppression remains active beyond the window or we see any regressions."
